findings.note: realCodexExec never sets cmd.Stderr, so the Codex CLI's stderr is discarded to /dev/null. On a nonzero exit the only diagnosis surfaced is judge/codex.go:69 'codex exited N' with no message from the process, making CLI-provider failures (bad model id, auth expiry, sandbox refusal) opaque. Capturing stderr into a capped buffer and folding it into the transport error would cost nothing in the success path.

evidence.note: cmd.Stdout is set, cmd.Stderr is left nil
error text is exit code only, no process output

findings.note: A codex process killed by a signal (context deadline/cancel via exec.CommandContext, or an OOM kill) returns an *exec.ExitError whose ExitCode() is -1, so realCodexExec reports (code=-1, err=nil) and codexJudge renders CodeJudgeTransport 'codex exited -1' rather than a cancellation/timeout error. Not a hang risk (the retry ladder selects on ctx.Done at judge.go:534), but the failure is misclassified for the operator and for any exit-code-based triage.

evidence.note: errors.As(*exec.ExitError) branch returns ee.ExitCode() with a nil error, which is -1 for signal death
ctx.Done is honoured by the retry ladder, bounding the impact

findings.note: newHTTPClient does an unchecked type assertion http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport), which panics if any imported package replaces http.DefaultTransport (instrumentation/record-replay libraries do). This contradicts the RealDeps doc comment 'binds every seam to its real implementation and nothing else; it cannot fail'. The clone-and-nil-Proxy idiom is the one prior artifact review asked for, so this is a robustness/doc-accuracy note, not a design objection; a comma-ok assertion with a fresh &http.Transport{} fallback closes it.

evidence.note: RealDeps doc comment claims it cannot fail

findings.note: The adjudicate 'real bug' rule is now encoded twice in package kind: kind.Decision computes is_real AND confidence >= AdjudicateThreshold for the diff/report path, while the live adjudicate executor recomputes v.ParseError == "" && v.Decision && v.Confidence >= AdjudicateThreshold. The two are consistent today (both treat an absent confidence as 0), but the executor also requires an empty ParseError, which Decision cannot see; a future change to either arm can drift silently and make a diff report disagree with the run it describes. Extracting one predicate would remove the duplication.
